cells.tense: The reading is landing right now, and it is telling you where to go.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Give one thing that's drawing you a step before the week closes. Name what you felt on the way — not what it meant, just what it felt like.
cells.core:
You catch the shape of things early. A few signals gather together and something organizes itself, and the understanding is already sharper than the words you'd use for it. Some of what you see is about where you want to go — a light that pulls at you and keeps pulling, not a guess you invented.

The pull doesn't come with a feeling attached. You can read the shape of a thing and still have no idea what touching it would feel like, and that gap is where you stall. Move a little toward one of those before the week ends. What you feel on the way in tells you more than another pass of thinking does — the light gets closer, and you find out whether the draw holds.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape early, and it points at something real.
cells.verb: reading the shape beneath things until the way ahead sharpens into a line worth walking
cells.place: the ledge between what is and the light that pulls — close to it, not yet arrived

cells.tense: Tomorrow's version of this is already decided, and you're living as if it arrived.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Choose the call you already trust and move on it before the day ends. Skip the explaining, and once you've moved, don't reopen it.
cells.core:
You read a situation quickly and then get ahead of it — deciding what it means before it has finished happening, moving as if the answer were already settled. The light ahead gets less interesting than your certainty about it. Plans thicken while the actual step thins out, and the people beside you receive decisions instead of company.

What you trust arrives complete, and it doesn't need defending. Choose one call you've already made — no research, no more angles — and move on it that same day. Skip the explaining, especially to whoever would be steadied by it. The clarity you already have carries its own weight; saying its name is the extra part. Once you move without the announcement, you find out what the read was worth.
cells.sheetLine: You've already decided what tomorrow means, and you're living there.
cells.verb: reading the shape beneath things until the way ahead sharpens into a line worth walking
cells.place: the ledge between what is and the light that pulls — close to it, not yet arrived

cells.tense: You were there when the understanding came, and you have stayed beside it since.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: Bring what you understand to one person who needs it. Say it in your own words, at their pace, and stay until the back-and-forth runs out.
cells.core:
You understand things. The quiet forming of a pattern still works in you, and the sense of where you're headed has gone still — the direction is where it was, and you've stopped pointing at it. You stand as someone who gets it, and the getting-it hasn't turned into anything that changes where you are.

Meaning moves when it's carried between people. Choose one piece of understanding — not your best insight, the one you'd actually use — and bring it to someone who needs it. Put it in your own words, at their pace, and keep the exchange open both ways; if their version is better, take it. What happens between you is where the understanding starts leading again, and where the draw underneath it starts pulling you toward something you can walk to.
cells.sheetLine: You understand it, and you've stopped walking toward anything.
cells.verb: reading the shape beneath things until the way ahead sharpens into a line worth walking
cells.place: the ledge between what is and the light that pulls — close to it, not yet arrived

cells.tense: The pattern is being read by you right now, and your account of it leaves you out.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Catch the moment a pattern settles and you see the way. Before filing it under what you're like, sit with it for a breath and notice the pull.
cells.core:
The recognition does work you don't count as yours. A few things happen and the shape of them comes clear, and by the time you'd describe it, it sounds like something you noticed rather than something you did. It shapes what you do next. The account you carry doesn't include it, so it keeps running as if no one were home.

There was a pull first — a small want toward something, with a read attached. Watch for the moment the pattern settles, the one where you see the way to go. Sit with it for a breath before filing it under what you're like. Naming that the pull showed up costs nothing, and it is the part that has been going unclaimed.
cells.sheetLine: The reading is happening. Your own account of it leaves you out.
cells.verb: reading the shape beneath things until the way ahead sharpens into a line worth walking
cells.place: the ledge between what is and the light that pulls — close to it, not yet arrived
